grammar.title: GRAMMAR
grammar.rule_explanation: Bu modulda Past Simple o'tkir voqeaning ketma-ketligini, simptomlarning qachon boshlanganini va aniq vaqtga bog'langan klinik voqealarni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Time expressions esa tarixni aniq timeline ko'rinishida tuzishga yordam beradi. Acute history-takingda Past Simple ko'pincha voqealarni ketma-ket joylashtirish uchun ishlatiladi:
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu modulda Past Simple o'tkir voqeaning ketma-ketligini, simptomlarning qachon boshlanganini va aniq vaqtga bog'langan klinik voqealarni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Time expressions esa tarixni aniq timeline ko'rinishida tuzishga yordam beradi. Acute history-takingda Past Simple ko'pincha voqealarni ketma-ket joylashtirish uchun ishlatiladi:
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple используется для завершённых событий в прошлом. В этом диалоге он особенно важен, потому что врач восстанавливает точную временную последовательность начала инсульта. Главное: при остром инсульте пациент должен уметь рассказать события в правильной временной последовательности. Поэтому Past Simple + time expressions являются центральным языковым инструментом этого модуля.
grammar.rule_explanation_en:
WH-question: What/When + did + subject + V1...? → What time did the ambulance arrive? When I stood up, my right leg felt weak and I nearly fell.
Why: Two past events within the same episode.
grammar.structure_pattern: When did + Subject + start? | Subject + V2 + (ago / yesterday / last night)

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Please tell me exactly what happened and what time the symptoms began.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I noticed something was wrong at about 7:15 this morning while I was having breakfast.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: What was the first symptom?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: My right hand suddenly became weak. I dropped my cup and couldn't pick it up again.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: What happened after that?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: A few minutes later, I tried to speak to my wife, but my words came out strangely. Relative: His face also looked uneven on the right side.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you understand what your wife was saying to you?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I understood everything, but I couldn't express myself properly.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you have any difficulty walking?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. When I stood up, my right leg felt weak and I nearly fell. Nurse: His current blood pressure is 182 over 96. He is alert but has expressive speech difficulty and right-sided weakness.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you lose consciousness at any stage?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I remained conscious throughout.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you develop a sudden severe headache?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: No.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you notice any visual disturbance?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: My vision became blurred for a few minutes, but then it improved.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: What time did the ambulance arrive? Relative: At approximately 7:45.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. The exact time of symptom onset is crucial because some stroke treatments are time-dependent.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Is it possible to treat the blockage?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Potentially, yes. First we need urgent brain imaging to determine whether this is an ischemic stroke or a haemorrhage. Nurse: I'll arrange immediate transfer for CT imaging and continue neurological observations.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: We also need to establish the last-known-well time and confirm whether there are any contraindications to reperfusion therapy.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: What happens if the scan shows a blood clot?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: If it confirms an eligible ischemic stroke, the stroke team will assess whether thrombolysis or mechanical thrombectomy is appropriate. Relative: And if there is bleeding?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: The management would be completely different, which is why imaging must be obtained before we make that decision.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I just want to know what we can do.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: We are moving quickly because every minute can matter in acute stroke.

tests.question: Which of the following is the grammatically and clinically standard question to ask about the duration of symptoms?
tests.option_a: How long do you having this symptom?
tests.option_b: How long has this condition been bothering you?
tests.option_c: Since what time you have this problem?
tests.option_d: How many days you are feeling pain?
tests.explanation: Klinik anamnezda davomiylikni so'rash uchun Present Perfect Continuous ('How long has... been bothering you?') to'g'ri shakl hisoblanadi.

tests.question: When evaluating acute pain, what is the best phrasing to assess pain character?
tests.option_a: Is your pain bad or very bad?
tests.option_b: Can you describe the pain—is it sharp, dull, throbbing, or aching?
tests.option_c: Why do you have sharp pain today?
tests.explanation: Og'riq xarakterini aniqlashda shifokor ochiq va taklif qiluvchi variantlar (sharp, dull, throbbing, aching) beradi.
